solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Some worth reshipping, separate wheat from chaff (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the next words are used

annotation.surface: A grain merchant weighs up whether it's worth sending the harvest back.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two words, which is where hidden answers like to sit.
annotation.definitionFit: To thresh is to beat grain so the wheat comes away from the chaff.

entries.clue: Mysterious man’s clue for America (5,3)

indicatorNotes.Mysterious: the letters that follow are in a puzzling, jumbled state

annotation.surface: A detective puzzles over the clue a strange man left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive's S counts as a letter of the fodder; the apostrophe is ignored.
annotation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government.

entries.clue: It seems solver has left Trappist brotherhood? That sounds a lot better (3,3’2,7) (3,5,7)

annotation.definition: It seems solver has left Trappist brotherhood? That sounds a lot better

blocks.clueFragment: It seems solver has left Trappist brotherhood?
blocks.note: Trappist monks keep a vow of silence, so anyone who has left the order has started speaking
the everyday phrase of approval when an offer improves

annotation.surface: A former monk gives up his vow of silence, and the setter welcomes the change.
annotation.walkthrough: Trappist monks keep near-total silence, so a solver who has left the order is at last speaking: YOU (the solver) ARE TALKING NOW. The phrase is also everyday approval of a better offer.
annotation.definitionFit: "Now you're talking" is what people say when a suggestion sounds a lot better than the last one.

entries.clue: Innocent child with publicity on a sensual dance (7)

blocks.note: a lamb is a gentle, innocent child

annotation.surface: A child star is exploited by publicity for a racy dance routine.
annotation.walkthrough: In this across-style charade the pieces simply run in the order the clue gives them.
annotation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian dance famous for its close, hip-swaying moves.

entries.clue: Rousing anthem for a hymn felt sad, potentially (4,2,2,7)

indicatorNotes.potentially: the letters could potentially form something else

annotation.surface: A mournful hymn could, with the right arrangement, become a stirring anthem.
annotation.walkthrough: Land of My Fathers is the national anthem of Wales, famously belted out at rugby internationals.
annotation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers (Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau) is the rousing Welsh national anthem.

entries.clue: Furniture department (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a bureau is one piece of furniture, not furniture in general

blocks.note: an administrative office, as in the Federal one of Investigation

annotation.surface: A sign in a department store points to the furniture section.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it is a shop floor; split in two it is a desk and an office.
annotation.definitionFit: A bureau is both a writing desk and an administrative department.

entries.clue: Maybe Vincent or Kelly‘s inheritable factor (4)

blocks.note: the rock'n'roll singer Vincent and the dancer Kelly share a first name

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a talent was inherited from a Vincent or a Kelly.
annotation.walkthrough: Vincent and Kelly look like surnames of relatives; what they share is the first name Gene.
annotation.definitionFit: A gene is the unit by which a trait is passed from parent to child.

entries.clue: Global superpower ignoring a feature (4)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: the A is left out of the word

blocks.note: the final A of the superpower is dropped

annotation.surface: Commentary on a superpower overlooking some aspect of world affairs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Feature' sounds like an aspect of policy, but here it is a facial feature.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chin is one of the parts that make up a face, each called a feature.

entries.clue: Starters of organic vegetables and eggs (3)

indicatorNotes.Starters of: take the starting letters of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A healthy menu: organic vegetable starters, then eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starters' reads as the first course of a meal. The 'and' does double duty: its A is the last letter, and it joins wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural for eggs, used in biology.

entries.clue: First twelve hours of the day spent pleasantly occupied (6)

blocks.clueFragment: First twelve hours of the day
blocks.note: a.m., the hours from midnight to noon

annotation.surface: Someone describes a contented morning spent happily busy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one diary line; the break falls after 'spent', not before 'the day'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone kept happily entertained is pleasantly occupied.

entries.clue: Associate following on, in fact (6)

annotation.surface: A business partner keeps things going, as a matter of fact.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following on' looks like one phrase meaning continuing; split it, and 'following' just says which piece comes second. RE for 'on' is the memo-heading 'regarding'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both are adverbs of emphasis, as in "it was, in fact, the butler".

entries.clue: Sign socialist coerced (8)

blocks.note: a badge is a sign or emblem
a red is a socialist or communist

annotation.surface: A left-winger was pressured into signing something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun BADGE.
annotation.definitionFit: To be badgered is to be pestered or pressured into doing something.

entries.clue: Perhaps note Alpine film? (3,5,2,5)

blocks.note: a single note is an example of what music makes you hear
the 1965 musical set in the Austrian Alps

annotation.surface: A critic jots down a reminder about a film set in the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' pretends to be a memo; 'Perhaps' signals that a note is just one example of the sound music makes.
annotation.definitionFit: The Sound of Music is the Julie Andrews film set around Salzburg and the Alps.

entries.clue: Watering hole cool, by the sound of it (3)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: the answer is heard, not spelt, like the word for cool

annotation.surface: A trendy bar gets a lukewarm verdict.
annotation.walkthrough: IN meaning fashionable is said exactly like INN.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang idiom: a watering hole is any place people go to drink, like a pub or an old coaching house.

entries.clue: Thrown out in cricket (7)

blocks.note: the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while the batsman is out of his ground

annotation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a batsman run out by a throw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thrown out' reads as one cricket phrase; the split falls after 'Thrown', which means baffled. Stumped is a way of being dismissed in cricket, by the wicketkeeper.
annotation.definitionFit: Thrown and stumped both mean confused, and stumped is a cricket dismissal.

entries.clue: Drink a drop, but not all (3)

indicatorNotes.but not all: not all of the word is used: its last letter goes

blocks.note: the salty drop from a crying eye; not all of it, so its last letter goes

annotation.surface: Someone asks for just a drop of their drink, not a full cup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A drop' is a teardrop here, not a small measure of the drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the everyday British brew is one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Leader of government on the right, I own my rogue state (7)

indicatorNotes.Leader of: take the first letter of government
indicatorNotes.on the right: the G goes at the right-hand end
indicatorNotes.rogue: the letters of I OWN MY go astray

annotation.surface: A right-wing head of government boasts of owning a rogue state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the right' sounds political, but it only places the G at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this western US state is one of fifty.

entries.clue: Put off, something smelly hanging in cupboard? (8)

blocks.note: to shelve a plan, storing it away until later
a pungent ball of repellent hung among clothes

annotation.surface: Someone is repelled by a stink coming from the wardrobe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as disgusted by the smell; it actually means postponed.
annotation.definitionFit: To mothball is to postpone; a mothball is a strong-smelling ball kept among clothes.

entries.clue: Learner ending on stage in debut, young actress (7)

indicatorNotes.ending on: take the final letter of stage
indicatorNotes.in: L and E go inside the word for debut

annotation.surface: A young actress, learning the ropes, finishes her stage debut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Debut' is the word that gets filled, not the start of the phrase; and 'ending on stage' means its final letter, not a closing performance.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym with a diminutive: the -LET ending makes a little star, a young actress on the rise.

entries.clue: Thrilling picture, killer drawing? (5,10)

annotation.surface: An exciting painting turns out to be a sketch by a murderer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is a film, not a painting, and 'drawing' means pulling towards, not a sketch.
annotation.definitionFit: Fatal Attraction is a thriller film, and a deadly pull is literally a fatal attraction.

entries.clue: Thoroughfare in ’arbour, extremely unremarkable (6)

indicatorNotes.’: the apostrophe marks a dropped H, as in Cockney speech
indicatorNotes.extremely: take only the extreme letters of unremarkable

blocks.note: harbour = HAVEN; drop the H as the clue does

annotation.surface: A street by the docks is described as dull.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ’arbour tells you to drop the H, and the same goes for its synonym HAVEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a broad, often tree-lined, street is a thoroughfare.

entries.clue: Done, lavatory emptied too (6)

indicatorNotes.emptied: the middle of lavatory is removed

annotation.surface: Finished in the toilet, which has been flushed too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Too' in the surface means also; as the definition it means excessively.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of excessively: "too careful" and "overly careful" say the same.

entries.clue: Dasher uncovered – or Comet? (8)

blocks.note: someone who dashes naked through a crowd
a comet streaks across the sky

annotation.surface: Two of Santa's reindeer, Dasher and Comet, with one of them exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: Dasher and Comet are both Santa's reindeer, which hides that one is a naked runner and the other a streak of light.
annotation.definitionFit: A streaker dashes naked, and a comet streaks through the sky.

entries.clue: A little testy, petulant sort (4)

indicatorNotes.A little: only a little of the next words is used

annotation.surface: A description of a slightly grumpy, sulky person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is the noun meaning kind, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both nouns mean a kind or category, as in "not my sort".

entries.clue: Language barrier initially breaks where translated (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of barrier
indicatorNotes.breaks: the B breaks into the other letters
indicatorNotes.translated: WHERE is turned into another arrangement

annotation.surface: A language barrier first shows itself where something is being translated.
annotation.walkthrough: B goes inside the rearranged WHERE: HE(B)REW. 'Translated' fits the surface so well it hides its job.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the language of the Old Testament and of modern Israel.

entries.clue: Economic recovery finished, go! (6)

annotation.surface: A recovery is announced, the downturn is finished, and it's all systems go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' reads as a command; it is the noun, a turn.
annotation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement, especially in the economy.

entries.clue: Drop a brick in drained river on head of eel (3)

indicatorNotes.drained: river is emptied of its middle letters
indicatorNotes.on: the E sits on, before, the RR
indicatorNotes.head of: take the first letter of eel

annotation.surface: Someone drops a brick into a dried-up riverbed, landing on an eel's head.
annotation.walkthrough: To drop a brick is a British idiom for making a tactless blunder, not a literal brick.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: dropping a brick means making a clumsy social blunder, which is to make a mistake.

entries.clue: Sit around when money’s short (4)

indicatorNotes.short: the word for money is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: lolly is British slang for money; cut short, it loses its Y

annotation.surface: Idleness sets in when funds run low.
annotation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for money; with its tail cut short it leaves LOLL.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to sprawl lazily is to sit around doing nothing.
